scope: Home album entry/collection metadata preparation and store entry/scroll catalog preparation; existing UI and behavior preserved
changes: Reuse already chronological home metadata; stable favorite partition uses one output list instead of separately sorted favorite/nonfavorite lists.
Collection compares immutable Album object identity and reuses its source snapshot on favorite-only updates; in-place list edits, deletions and owner changes still invalidate prepared data.

Use bounded published/retired/product identity indexes instead of per-template catalog scans and temporary authored lists. Canonical preview/artwork still requires the identical published document builder.

Merge favorite metadata in one catalog traversal using a temporary index limited to published IDs. Return the canonical object when favorite metadata is unchanged, preserving artwork identity during refresh.

Store reuses a single current-catalog price map and recommendation widget between pagination/comparison updates. Provider, favorite and filter changes invalidate the current data; hidden stores postpone preparation until visible.

reviewed: No new image, document, layer, widget-context or transport caches in global identity indexes; only fixed IDs/product strings or existing canonical object references.

Price/recommendation memoization is screen-instance scoped, retains one current snapshot, replaces prior data and releases with the existing state lifecycle. No timers, observers or requests were added.
Source list copying/sorting never mutates the parent album list. Immutable object checks detect updated content even when IDs remain the same.
Favorite merge keeps the first matching duplicate row; free/paid tier, pricing, catalog order, canonical lazy builder and server-ID fallback are unchanged.
Existing image decode limits, preview worker gates, memory-pressure cleanup and photo recovery sources were not modified.
Recommendation reuse is local to StoreScreen; the public TemplateCuration widget continues to process updated mutable inputs as before.

coverage: Sorted/unsorted/empty albums, draft exclusion, equal/invalid dates, favorites, deletion, edited same-ID objects, in-place mutation and account switch.
5,000 albums share large undecoded document text while metadata preparation preserves ordering and object identity.
Every published ID, free/paid/retired product identity, unknown server IDs and different-builder impostors; identity checks do not invoke custom document builders.
Catalog merge traverses 2,133 source rows once and preserves first duplicate favorite row; unchanged metadata preserves canonical object identity.

Instrumented 530-row price catalog is traversed once across pagination and curation reuse. Updated activation replaces recommendation candidates. Hidden updates perform no store indexing until resumed.

limits: The full set is not green: 17 existing failures were reproduced before and after this change and remain open. No assertions were weakened or existing tests edited to hide them.

Identity indexes add small bounded metadata tables; they do not retain extra image bytes or materialize documents. Real-device peak memory and FPS were not measured, so this review cannot claim zero native leaks or frame drops.
Unit/widget tests use controlled provider fixtures, not live purchases or backend writes.
